sections.heading: What a No Insurance Ticket Means Under Texas Law
paragraphs: Texas requires every driver to carry liability coverage and to prove it when an officer asks. When you can't, the citation reads "FMFR" — Failure to Maintain Financial Responsibility, Transportation Code 601.191. It is a Class C misdemeanor, fine-only, but the fine range is higher than almost any other traffic offense: $175 to $350 for a first offense, before court costs. Repeat offenses carry a higher range and can bring a license and registration suspension.

In El Paso, FMFR tickets usually arrive as a second citation. An El Paso Police officer stops you on Montana Avenue for speeding, asks for insurance, and the card in the glovebox is expired or the app won't load. Now you have two tickets from one stop, and the insurance ticket is the expensive one. The same thing happens with DPS troopers on I-10 and Sheriff's deputies in the county, where the case lands in a Justice of the Peace court.

Paying the ticket is a guilty plea and a conviction on your DPS record. This page is general information, not legal advice about your case — but the practical rule is simple: never pay an FMFR ticket without talking to a lawyer first.

sections.heading: Had Insurance at the Time of the Stop? The Ticket Usually Goes Away
paragraphs: The most common FMFR case we see is a driver who was fully insured and simply couldn't prove it on the roadside. The policy was in a spouse's name, the renewal card never got printed, or the phone died. Texas law treats this as a defense: show the court a policy that was in force on the date and time of the citation, covering that vehicle, and the charge is generally dismissed. Many courts call this the "show proof later" rule.

Doing it right matters. The court wants a declarations page or an insurer's letter that states the effective dates and lists the vehicle — not just the wallet card. In El Paso Municipal Court the proof typically has to be filed before the appearance date, and some judges charge a small administrative fee for the dismissal. We confirm the policy dates match the citation and file the proof with our notice of appearance so the case is set for dismissal on the first docket.

What if the policy lapsed a few days before the stop? Harder, but not hopeless. Prosecutors in El Paso County know most lapses are a missed autopay. If you have since reinstated coverage, we can often negotiate a deferred disposition or an amended charge so the FMFR conviction never reaches your record.

sections.heading: Why Insurers Punish an FMFR Conviction So Hard
paragraphs: Insurance companies read a no-insurance conviction as proof that you drove without coverage, which puts you in a higher-risk tier than a driver with a plain speeding ticket. The premium increase on renewal is often larger than the fine itself, it follows you for three years, and some carriers decline to renew at all.

Then there is the SR-22. After an FMFR conviction, Texas can require you to file an SR-22 certificate of financial responsibility for two years to keep or reinstate your license. Not every insurer offers SR-22 filings, and those that do charge for it. Let it lapse and DPS suspends the license, which is how a $250 ticket turns into a driving while license invalid charge at the next stop.

sections.heading: FMFR Tickets From the County, Horizon City, Socorro and Beyond
paragraphs: Who wrote the ticket decides where it's filed. El Paso Police citations go to Municipal Court downtown. A DPS state trooper ticket on I-10 or Loop 375, or a Sheriff's deputy ticket in the Lower Valley, lands in an El Paso County Justice of the Peace precinct. Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint and Anthony each run their own municipal court with its own approach to FMFR cases.

Our flat fee is $59 in El Paso Municipal Court and $69 in JP and the smaller city courts, covering the full case from filing through disposition. Not sure where your ticket is? Use the free ticket and warrant lookup and we'll find it.

sections.heading: What to Do Right Now After a No Insurance Ticket
paragraphs: First, find out whether you were covered. Log into your insurer's app or call the agent and ask for a declarations page showing the policy period. If the policy was active, save that document — it is the whole case. If it wasn't, get coverage today; prosecutors treat a driver who is now insured very differently from one who still isn't.

Then check the appearance date and don't let it pass. A missed date means a failure-to-appear charge and a warrant on top of the FMFR. If it already passed, read our warrant recall page and call us the same day.

faqs.q: I had insurance but couldn't find my card. Will the ticket be dismissed?
faqs.a: In most cases, yes. If the policy was in force at the time of the stop and covered the vehicle, El Paso courts generally dismiss the FMFR charge once proof is filed. We verify the dates on your declarations page and file it with the court so you don't have to appear.

faqs.q: How much is a no insurance ticket in El Paso?
faqs.a: The statutory fine for a first offense under Transportation Code 601.191 is $175 to $350, plus court costs. The far larger cost is what a conviction does to your insurance rates for three years, which is why we recommend fighting it for a flat $59–$69.

faqs.q: Will I need an SR-22 after an FMFR ticket?
faqs.a: An SR-22 is typically tied to a conviction, not the citation itself. If the ticket is dismissed or resolved through deferred disposition with no conviction, the SR-22 requirement usually never arises — one of the main reasons not to just pay.

faqs.q: My policy lapsed a few days before the stop. Do I have any options?
faqs.a: Yes. Get coverage reinstated right away, then let us negotiate. With current proof of insurance we can often secure a deferred disposition or an amended charge instead of an FMFR conviction.

faqs.q: Do I have to go to court for a no insurance ticket?
faqs.a: Usually not when you hire us. We file the notice of appearance, submit your proof of insurance or negotiate at the pretrial docket, and report the result. You would only appear if the case went to trial, which is rare.

faqs.q: I got a no insurance ticket from a DPS trooper on I-10. Is that different?
faqs.a: The law is the same, but the court is different. Trooper and Sheriff's citations are filed in an El Paso County Justice of the Peace precinct rather than Municipal Court, and our flat fee there is $69.
